predecessors.name: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Modena and Reggio, whose duke Hercules III 'fled to Venice to escape the French advance'

predecessors.name: Papal States
predecessors.text: the Papal Legations of Bologna and Ferrara

successors.name: Cisalpine Republic
successors.text: the provinces of Modena, Bologna, Ferrara and Reggio Emilia

ledger.x: 16 October 1796: the congress of Modena creates the Cispadane Republic.
October 1796: Modena and Reggio leave their duke.
29 June 1797: the Cispadane joins the Cisalpine.
29 June 1797: the Cispadane Republic ceases; its land passes to the Cisalpine Republic.

wars.name: Italian campaign of 1796-1797
wars.outcome: Napoleon's army took Modena and the Papal Legations from their rulers; they became the Cispadane Republic and then, on 29 June 1797, part of the Cisalpine Republic.

certainty.note: The republic is four provinces named at a congress; the page gives no boundary and its territory was settled only as French armies took it.
